newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli seaports hit briefly by strike.
newsitem.headline: Israeli seaports hit briefly by strike.

text.p: Workers briefly closed Israeli seaports on Tuesday but unions called off a planned general strike to give the government time to reconsider austerity measures in the 1997 budget.
A spokesman for the ports and railways authority said the Ashdod and Haifa ports reopened after a work stoppage during the morning. He said he knew of no plans to resume the strike.

Strikes by more than a quarter of a million workers crippled large sectors of Israel's economy on Monday, the fourth day of strikes in protest at Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's proposed economic measures.

Parliament was due to vote on the 1997 budget early on Wednesday. The decision to lift the general strike threat was taken late on Monday after parliament rejected a proposal to eliminate a special tax credit for working women.
A spokeswoman at the strike headquarters of the Histadrut trade union federation said on Tuesday afternoon: "There's nothing, everyone's working."
Netanyahu had blasted the strikes called by the Histadrut as irresponsible and "baseless".
